reviews.review:
Super fun coop shooter, and if you are a fan of Alien this game is a must. The levels are different and interesting, and the player base are friendly and helpful even at lower levels. 

Get two friends together and the three of you can have a great time! Worth even if you only plan to go trough once

Pro:
-Original Soundtrack and Sounds from the Movies
-Very true to the source material in many aspects
-Pretty graphics and levels
-Intense action
-Lots of cosmetics (can also be found in hidden crates in every level)
-Lots of fun weapons (also from the movies, like the smartgun or flamethrower)
-Adequate Difficulty (even on casual you'll get sweaty from hordes of Xenos swarming you)
-Bots are pretty good if you can't find human teammates

Con:
-Sometimes a bit janky
-Only 4 Campaigns with 3 missions each (another Campaign as DLC)
-Gameplay and animations remind a little bit too much of Fortnite (UE Vanilla animations) (i guess the devs got lazy here and didnt feel the need to make new ones)

Aliens: Fireteam Elite takes the enemy mechanics of LFD and the gameplay of fortnite and slams it together into a fun alien shoot em up. It's not perfect but it's quite fun especially if you like the movies. Get it on sale. 7/10

TLDR: The game is a clunky, boring, highly linear mess and I'm thankful I paid nothing but time for it.

Got this game as a gift. Never would've bought it with my own funds. It's a solid 2.5/5. Truly arcade style with the most minimum amount of things to do and very lackluster combat followed by its less than poor enemy construction. Something about the very stiff enemies, very predictable, and often times more of a haunted house scare than an actual threat. I can walk past them most times with zero issue. It's a very stagnant to the point game with every mission being the same and zero replayability unless you plan to run a different class which adds no real change to playstyle even with using different gear setups.

It's a fun game and great with a few friends. If you're an Alien fan, this will be a bonus. The class system is fun, and the novel way of arranging perks in available slots, and trying to be efficient and clever with their combinations is quite good. The character customisation is moderate, but plenty good enough. Gunplay is reasonable but nothing revolutionary. There's cool nods to the various movies, and a decent amount of gameplay variety from the clever challenge card system (player-elected wagers prior to mission start, with lots of random effects and bonuses/penalties). The campaign is short - only 12 missions - and there's no endless mode or random levels, so you're stuck replaying the same stuff again and again. But the gameplay is fun enough, and if you can pick this up for under a tenner, I recommend it.
